messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 45-year-old woman comes to the physician because of fatigue and irregular menstrual cycles for the past year. She also complains of recurrent sinus infections. During the past 6 months, she has had increased urinary frequency and swelling of her feet. She has also had difficulty lifting her 3-year-old niece for the past 3 weeks. She was recently diagnosed with depression. She works as a medical assistant. The patient has smoked one half-pack of cigarettes daily for 25 years and drinks four beers on the weekends. Her only medication is escitalopram. She is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 79 kg (175 lb); BMI is 31 kg/m2. She appears tired. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 80/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 140/82 mm Hg. Physical examinations shows neck obesity and an enlarged abdomen. Examination of the skin shows multiple bruises on her arms and legs. There is generalized weakness and atrophy of the proximal muscles. Laboratory studies show:
Serum
Na+ 150 mEq/L
K+ 3.0 mEq/L
Cl- 103 mEq/L
HCO3- 30 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen 19 mg/dL
Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL
Glucose 136 mg/dL
A 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test shows a serum cortisol of 167 nmol/L (N < 50) and a 24-hour urinary cortisol is 425 μg (N < 300 μg). Serum ACTH is 169 pg/mL (N = 7–50). Subsequently, a high-dose dexamethasone suppression test shows a serum cortisol level of 164 nmol/L (N < 50). Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?"

Options:
A. Adrenal carcinoma
B. Hypothyroidism
C. Pheochromocytoma
D. Small cell lung cancer
E. Adrenal adenoma

Correct answer: D. Small cell lung cancer

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is an endocrinology question about ectopic ACTH (Cushing syndrome) from small cell lung cancer; the depression and escitalopram are incidental distractors."}
